sentences.text: Hardness crept up to 240 ppm overnight — someone check whether the crushed coral bag split. Dim lights keep the wild bettas calm, so we work by headlamp when netting out pairs. Nobody warned me that angelfish eat their first three clutches before figuring out parenthood. I mark each spawning jar's lid with tape: date, pair number, hardness at laying. Eggs stuck to the heater cord again, which means scraping and praying half survive the move. He logs GH and KH in a spiral notebook, one column per shelf, dated in pencil. Every runt gets fed to the bichir; sentiment doesn't pay for fish food. Her ledger shows which pairings threw long fins and which threw nothing worth keeping. Fry from batch eleven took powdered egg yolk at dawn and again at three. Records indicate the corydoras deposited eggs on the glass within six hours of the cool-water change. Water changes happen Sundays: twenty percent for growouts, ten for anything still at wriggler stage. Wrigglers clung to the slate for two days before lifting off in one silver cloud. At 6.4 pH the rams finally spawned, after months of stubborn refusal at 7.2. The kribensis pair claimed the coconut cave again, fanning eggs before the lights even warmed up. A siphon hose, a brine shrimp hatchery, and a bucket of aged water — my whole morning, basically. Conditioning took two weeks of blackworms before the female finally plumped up enough to set. Do buyers ever ask about the culls? Never — they only want the show-quality males. Along all four shelves the sponge filters gurgle softly, a sound she stopped hearing years ago. Check the spawning mop tomorrow; the ricefish were chasing hard through it all afternoon. Under the dim red bulb, the pleco female stayed wedged in her cave for nine days straight. Honestly, half our overtime comes from grinding out sloppy tack welds the day shift leaves behind. Third rejection this week on bay two's seams—somebody check that wire feed. Her ultrasonic probe traced the seam twice; the second pass found the void the first had missed. Sparks rained off the hull plate while two welders argued, through their visors, about last night's match. Under the floodlights, the half-finished chassis looked less like a war machine and more like a beached steel whale. The shift supervisor taped the rejection slip to the chassis and told nobody to touch it until the metallurgist arrived. All armored side panels shall be degreased, inspected for lamination defects, and logged before entering the assembly line. Nine bare chassis sat in line for turret installation, but only one crane operator was scheduled before noon. Quality inspectors rejected fourteen hull plates on Tuesday after ultrasonic testing revealed porosity along the lower weld seams. A hairline crack in the mantlet casting sent the whole batch back to the foundry, three weeks of schedule gone. Watch the sling angle, Marek—if that turret assembly swings into the jig again, we lose the whole morning. Crane four to floor: lowering the turret in thirty seconds, clear the ring. Did anyone recalibrate the torque wrenches after the audit, or are we still guessing on the ring bolts? I've welded hull seams for eleven years, and my hands still shake a little when the crane passes overhead. Who signed off on this weld bead—it undercuts the armor plate nearly two millimeters at the corner? When the klaxon sounds, everything stops—welders lift their visors, the crane freezes mid-lift, and the floor goes quiet. Next quarter the plant will add a second overhead crane, so turret drops won't bottleneck the afternoon shift anymore. Procedure 41-C requires two inspectors to witness the seating of the turret race before any fasteners are installed. Rivas steadied the swaying turret with one gloved palm, guiding the crane operator down the last few centimeters. By dawn the third shift had ground down every rough seam on the glacis plates, leaving the bay smelling of scorched metal. What is the meaning of the word tank?
